does: The handler of the Osiris call StartChangeAppearance(Target). It resolves the character, refuses one whose reserved user id (+0x188) is the unassigned constant or that has no eoc::character_creation::AppearanceComponent, refuses while the bytes at +0x250 or +0x288 of esv::character_creation::System are set, and otherwise appends the pair (character entity, unassigned user id) to the system's request array at +0x4E8 (count at +0x4F4) and answers true. The session itself is made by the system later: a definition entity with eoc::character_creation::ChangeAppearanceDefinitionComponent and a session entity appear, and the client opens the widget CharacterChangeAppearance.

evidence.says: the registration of the Osiris game functions (bg3_dx11.exe+0x36B0C00) pairs the text StartChangeAppearance with this address; the body calls esv::StoryUtils::OsirisParamGUIDToCharacter, ecs::HasComponent of eoc::character_creation::AppearanceComponent, takes the system by TypeIndex of esv::character_creation::System and writes 16 bytes into the array at +0x4E8

a count-only probe during Osi.StartChangeAppearance(host) shows one call, from bg3_dx11.exe+0x38248AA; afterwards the server holds one entity with CCChangeAppearanceDefinition and CCDefinitionCommon, one with CCSessionCommon, ServerCCSessionOwner and CCDefinitionChangeAppearance, and the host's CCState.HasDummy reads true (false before)

the Toolkit's EoCServer.dll function with the same checks (a character, reserved for a player, the system's request) carries the text esv::OsirisGameFunctions::StartChangeAppearance and its source file OsirisGameFunctions.cpp in its assertions

questions.ask: which function of esv::character_creation::System reads the array at +0x4E8 and builds the session (the Toolkit exports RequestChangeAppearance and Update); a probe on the readers of +0x4E8 during Osi.StartChangeAppearance reaches it
